question: Can the failure of layer-local blur programs on deep SIRENs be derived, not just measured? Two statements: (T1) a characterisation of which dictionaries admit readout-only LSI programs; (T2) a weight-only, closed-form predictor of the first-order program's per-unit error, derived from the Jacobi-Anger expansion of sin(c + sum_i a_i sin theta_i) under independent phases.
T1_characterisation: For f = sum_j a_j phi_j + b with fixed dictionary functions phi_j: readout-only edits (a_j -> s_j a_j) implement every isotropic Gaussian blur exactly, for every readout, iff every phi_j has its spectrum on a single radius |k| = r_j; they implement every real LSI filter exactly iff every phi_j is a single sinusoid (spectrum on +-k_j). Proof: plane waves are the eigenfunctions of LSI operators; a function with two spectral components of different gain cannot be scaled by one factor; conversely single-shell functions are eigenfunctions of all isotropic filters. Consequence: the one-sine-layer SIREN is the unique sine-network depth at which the readout is LSI-programmable; a deeper unit sin(c_j + sum_i a_ij sin theta_i) has spectrum on all integer combinations sum_i n_i w_i, so it is single-shell only in the degenerate limit a_ij -> 0 (where only the fundamentals survive).
T2_predictor: With theta_i treated as independent uniform phases (exact in the limit of incommensurate frequencies over a large domain), E[sin(c+delta)] = sin c prod_k J0(a_k), E[sin^2(c+delta)] = 1/2 - 1/2 cos(2c) prod_k J0(2a_k), and the projection of sin(c+delta) on sin theta_i is 2 J1(a_i) prod_{k!=i} J0(a_k) cos c. The fundamental fraction F_j = sum_i 2 (J1(a_i) prod_{k!=i} J0(a_k) cos c)^2 / (E[sin^2] - E[sin]^2) is the share of a unit's AC energy carried by first harmonics of its inputs. It is 1 at a -> 0 and decays with the swing. Prediction: the measured per-unit relative error of the first-order blur program is a monotone function of 1 - F_j.
experiment: scripts/unit_spectra.py extended: per unit of the last sine layer, measured first-order program error (blur of the unit on a fine grid vs the unit recomputed with attenuated inputs) and F_j from the weights. Zoos: mnist_s32 (standard), mnist_s32_swing{0.5,1,2,4} and swing8_seed0, mnist_s32_lam1e-3 (about 7 x 640 units). Also the independent-phase approximation itself: predicted vs measured unit mean and variance.

predictions_frozen_before_running.T2a_rank: Across all units of all zoos pooled, Spearman(1 - F_j, measured first-order error) >= 0.8, and within the standard zoo alone >= 0.6.
predictions_frozen_before_running.T2b_scale: For units with F_j >= 0.9 the median measured first-order error is below 0.05 (relative); for F_j <= 0.3 it is above 0.5.
predictions_frozen_before_running.T2c_better_than_H: 1 - F_j predicts the first-order error better than the harmonic index H_j (higher pooled Spearman by at least 0.05).
predictions_frozen_before_running.T2d_independent_phase_ok: The independent-phase prediction of each unit's variance is within a factor 1.5 of the measured variance for at least 80% of units with H_j >= 1 (for tiny H the variance is tiny and ratios are unstable; excluded).
predictions_frozen_before_running.T1_numerical: On the standard zoo, no unit has more than 50% of its AC energy on a single radius shell of relative width 20%; on the shallow zoo every unit has 100%. (Restates the stage-02 spread measurement in the theorem's terms.)

decision_rule: If T2a-T2c hold, F_j (or 1 - F_j) replaces H as the paper's diagnostic and the swing bound is reinterpreted as a bound on 1 - F; T1 goes in as a proposition with the numerical illustration. If T2a fails, the independent-phase model is wrong for these frequencies and the next step is the exact harmonic enumeration on a subset of units.
